evals.prompt: Some people see "You're subscribed" on the newsletter page but never get an email. Check the signup flow in a real browser (Playwright for Node: require('playwright'); the app is node server.js). Write e2e/subscribe.test.js (node:test, starts the server itself) that fails while this bug exists, and write what you found to QA-REPORT.md. Don't fix the app.
evals.check: test -z "$(git status --porcelain -- server.js public package.json)" && test -s QA-REPORT.md && grep -q '422' QA-REPORT.md && test -s e2e/subscribe.test.js && if timeout 90 node --test e2e/subscribe.test.js >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'e2e test passes on the buggy app'; exit 1; fi && T=$(mktemp -d) && cp -r . "$T/w" && cd "$T/w" && node -e "const fs=require('fs');let s=fs.readFileSync('public/app.js','utf8');s=s.replace('await fetch(','const res = await fetch(').replace('    status.textContent = \"You\\'re subscribed','    if (!res.ok) { const b = await res.json().catch(() => ({})); status.textContent = \\'Could not subscribe: \\' + (b.error || res.status); return; }\n    status.textContent = \"You\\'re subscribed');if(!s.includes('res.ok'))process.exit(9);fs.writeFileSync('public/app.js',s)" && if ! timeout 90 node --test e2e/subscribe.test.js >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'e2e test still fails once the app checks res.ok'; exit 1; fi
expectations: The check command exits 0 (app unchanged; QA-REPORT.md mentions the 422; e2e/subscribe.test.js fails on the current app and passes once app.js checks res.ok)
The agent captured the failed request in the browser flow (the POST /api/subscribe returning 422 for an address with +) rather than only reading the code
QA-REPORT.md names the cause: public/app.js shows the success message without checking the response status, so server validation errors are hidden
The e2e test starts and stops the server and browser itself and asserts on what the user sees (the status text) for a rejected address
